diagnostic_evidence.quote: We make no assumptions on the dimensions $m$ and~$n$ of~$\ma$.

issues.failure_explanation: For a column submatrix obtained from an m-by-n matrix, the lower interlacing index depends on the number n-k of deleted columns, with zero padding when necessary; replacing it by min{m,n}-k+j is false when n>m. For example, with m=2,n=3,k=1, the displayed bound can require sigma_2(A) to be no larger than the norm of every selected column, which fails if one column is arbitrarily small while the other two keep sigma_2(A) bounded away from zero.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the lower index by the standard deletion interlacing bound, explicitly including the required zero-padding convention.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's general interlacing assertion is invalid for part of its advertised unrestricted dimension regime. Later uses involving a full-column-rank matrix and its own column submatrix can employ the correct specialized interlacing relation.
issues.title: The stated singular-value interlacing lower bound is false for wide matrices
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction to a standard inequality, and the later specialized uses can remain unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where inputs are rational numbers and the input size is measured in the number of bits.

issues.failure_explanation: The reduced matrix contains the irrational number 1/sqrt(3), whereas the paper explicitly adopts a Turing model whose numeric inputs are rational. Thus the claimed reduced instance is not an instance in the stated computational model, and its polynomial bit-size construction has not been established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate the reduction using rational matrix entries and rationally encoded decision thresholds, then rescale and rederive the affected optimal values and gaps while preserving the relevant unit-column or equal-column-norm hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: Every NP-hardness and inapproximability result based on this X3C construction lacks a valid polynomial-time reduction in the declared rational-input model.
issues.title: The X3C reductions violate the paper's rational-input computational model
issues.why_classification: The X3C architecture may be reusable, but a complete repair requires coordinated reformulation and recalculation across essentially all reductions rather than a single typographical change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the second factor is a scalar and contains the orthogonal project $\mP\equiv \mi-\hat{\mc}_k^T\hat{\mc}_k^{\dagger}$

issues.failure_explanation: For an m-by-k matrix, both \hat C_k^T and \hat C_k^dagger are k-by-m, so their displayed product is undefined. The Schur complement should involve the projector onto the orthogonal complement of range(\hat C_{k-1}), but neither the equation nor the subsequently defined projector expresses that object.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the malformed calculation by the correct Gram-matrix Schur complement, or by the equivalent Gram-Schmidt identity showing that adjoining a unit column multiplies volume by a residual norm at most one.
issues.overall_effect: The induction proving the constant volume gap is invalid as written, so its use to obtain the S-optimality gap is also unsupported.
issues.title: The volume induction uses dimensionally undefined Schur-complement expressions
issues.why_classification: A short standard local argument supplies exactly the intended monotonicity without changing the theorem's bound or proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
This follows from the assumption of $\mc$ having unit-norm
columns, so that 
$\sopt(\ms)=\vol(\mc)^{1/k}$, and from Theorem~\ref{t_vol}.

A PTAS is a polynomial
time algorithm such that for each $\epsilon>0$
 there exists a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation algorithm for minimization problems, and a $(1-\epsilon)$-approximation algorithm for maximization problems

issues.failure_explanation: Taking the kth root converts the constant volume gap into (2sqrt(2)/3)^(1/k), which tends to 1 as k grows. A PTAS only promises polynomial time for each fixed epsilon; the proof cannot choose epsilon depending on the input parameter k. Therefore the displayed variable-factor hardness does not imply the asserted absence of a PTAS.

failure_location.quote:
It is NP hard to approximate S-optimality maximization within a factor of 
$(2\sqrt{2}/3)^{1/k}$. Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS for S-optimality maximization.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish a gap bounded away from one independently of k, or withdraw the no-PTAS conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The variable-factor hardness claim may remain, but the paper's advertised no-PTAS result for S-optimality is unsupported.
issues.title: A k-dependent S-optimality gap does not rule out a PTAS
issues.why_classification: The available argument cannot preserve the principal no-PTAS guarantee; obtaining it requires a new gap construction or abandoning that conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Does $\ma$ have a submatrix $\mc\in\real^{m\times k}$ with 
$\|\mc^\dagger\|_F \le b$?

issues.failure_explanation: The decision problems quantify over all k-column submatrices without requiring rank k, but the lower-bound lemmas used by the reductions require full column rank. For a rank-deficient matrix, the Moore-Penrose inverse omits reciprocals of zero singular values, so these bounds can fail; for example, two identical unit columns have pseudo-inverse two-norm 1/sqrt(2), contradicting the claimed unit lower bound if rank is not imposed. The X3C no-case argument establishes overlap, not full rank of every candidate.

failure_location.quote: The proof for all the norms is the same as that of Theorem~\ref{t_voldec} but uses Lemma~\ref{l_pinv} instead.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Explicitly restrict every affected optimization and decision problem to full-column-rank selected submatrices and consistently state how infeasible rank-deficient selections are treated.
issues.overall_effect: The reductions do not establish their required no-case bounds for the stated feasible sets, and some condition-number objectives are undefined under the paper's own full-rank definition.
issues.title: Pseudo-inverse and condition-number reductions omit full-column-rank feasibility
issues.why_classification: The repair preserves a comparable full-rank subset-selection problem and the intended reductions, but materially changes the feasible-set quantifier across several central criteria.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
It is NP hard to approximate the Schatten $p$-norm minimization of the pseudo-inverse within a factor of 
$\sqrt{1+\tfrac{1}{4k}}$ for $p>2$. Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS for Schatten $p$-norm minimization of the pseudo-inverse.

It is NP hard to approximate Frobenius norm condition number minimization within a factor of 
$\sqrt{1+\tfrac{1}{4k}}$. Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS for Frobenius norm condition number minimization.

issues.failure_explanation: The factor sqrt(1+1/(4k)) tends to 1 with the input parameter k. Hardness at this input-dependent ratio does not contradict a PTAS, whose polynomial-time guarantee is only for each fixed approximation tolerance. The same invalid inference is repeated for Schatten p pseudo-inverse minimization and inherited by the Frobenius condition-number result.

failure_location.quote:
It is NP hard to approximate Frobenius norm minimization of the pseudo-inverse within a factor of 
$\sqrt{1+\tfrac{1}{4k}}$. Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS for Frobenius norm minimization of the pseudo-inverse.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must provide a constant gap independent of k for each criterion, or remove the no-PTAS conclusions.
issues.overall_effect: The derived k-dependent gaps may survive, but the claimed no-PTAS results for these three criteria are not established.
issues.title: Vanishing pseudo-inverse and Frobenius-condition gaps do not imply no PTAS
issues.why_classification: Preserving the advertised guarantees requires a new constant-gap reduction; otherwise three substantive no-PTAS claims must be abandoned.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Since all factors $\sigma_j(\mc)/\sigma_1(\mc)\leq 1$, (\ref{e_ortho}) can only 
hold if all factors $\sigma_j(\mc)/\sigma_1(\mc)=1$.
Hence, all singular values of $\mc$ are equal to~1

issues.failure_explanation: The product condition only implies that all singular values are equal to the same positive value, not that this value is one. For example, C=2I has relative volume one but does not have orthonormal columns.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, $\rvol(\mc) = 1$  if and only if the columns of $\mc$ are orthonormal.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that relative volume one is equivalent to C being a positive scalar multiple of a matrix with orthonormal columns, or add unit-norm columns as a hypothesis where orthonormality is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed scale-sensitive equality characterization is false. Uses restricted to unit-norm columns can recover orthonormality by adding that hypothesis.
issues.title: Relative volume one characterizes scaled isometries, not orthonormal columns
issues.why_classification: A short local correction gives the exact characterization and leaves the unit-column reductions intact.

issues.failure_explanation: From sigma_1(C)>=1 one gets k^(1/p)/sigma_1(C)<=k^(1/p), the reverse of the second displayed inequality. Thus the proof does not establish the claimed lower bound, although that bound can instead be obtained by convexity applied to the squared singular values.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the invalid estimate by a convexity or Lagrange-multiplier argument showing that, subject to the fixed sum of squared singular values, the sum of their negative pth powers is minimized when all singular values equal one.
issues.overall_effect: The supporting lemma for Schatten pseudo-inverse NP-hardness and related condition-number arguments is unproved as written.
issues.title: The pseudo-inverse Schatten lower bound is proved using a reversed inequality
issues.why_classification: The claim is recoverable by a short standard local argument with the same hypotheses and conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: For a block diagonal matrix, a Schatten q-norm is not the sum of the block Schatten q-norms unless q=1; its qth power is additive. The asserted lemma is directly false for C=I_2 partitioned into its two columns: the left side is 2^(2/p), while the right side is 2, and 2^(2/p)<2 for p>2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, the statement must be replaced by the correctly powered pinching inequality or otherwise substantially weakened.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised partitioned pseudo-inverse lower bound for Schatten p-norms is false, so that contribution is not established.
issues.title: The partitioned Schatten pseudo-inverse inequality is false
issues.why_classification: The formal claim itself fails even for the identity matrix, and preserving its stated additive squared-norm conclusion is impossible.
